svg.title: Make It, Sell It, or License It
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-01-licensing-model-fork; chapter number: 1; chart type: process_flow; title: Make It, Sell It, or License It; subtitle: The five-step fork practitioners walk before pitching a single licensee; caption: Licensing wins the consensus for inventors who want the licensee's money, staff and shelf space; inventRightTV contrasts an instant 20,000-store footprint with at least $250,000 floated to venture alone.; assumptions note: Step order follows the operator gates cited for Chapter Q1. Royalty bands are attributed claims (2 to 10% of wholesale per Patent Question, 3 to 5% and up to 10% per Patent pc, 5 to 20% per UpCounsel) and vary by industry.; note: Attributed to The Sourcing Gals, Patent Question, inventRightTV, UpCounsel, Patent pc, Licensing Consulting Group, Kauffman FoundersSchool and Michigan Engineering.; stages: step: 01; label: Lock a protectable element; value: Step 1; detail: The Sourcing Gals refuse further deal conversations until the technology is protected.; step: 02; label: Weigh venturing against licensing; value: Step 2; detail: Venturing meant floating at least $250,000 with retailers paying in 60 to 90 days (inventRightTV); Patent Question bars manufacturing without demand, margins, a sales channel and operating ability.; step: 03; label: Pitch as a product developer; value: Step 3; detail: Polished brochures, formal letters and prototypes; brokers paid on commission only and vetted through the United Inventors Association and Better Business Bureau (UpCounsel).; step: 04; label: Choose exclusivity and markets; value: Step 4; detail: Pick an exclusive partner carefully or demand non-exclusive where you hold market power (Patent pc); license human and pet markets at once (Licensing Consulting Group).; step: 05; label: Set minimums, then price; value: Step 5; detail: No license without annual minimums (Michigan Engineering); price comes last and is capped by the licensee's next best alternative (Kauffman FoundersSchool).

text.title: Make It, Sell It, or License It
text.tspan: Make It, Sell It, or License It

circle.title: step: 01; label: Lock a protectable element; value: Step 1; detail: The Sourcing Gals refuse further deal conversations until the technology is protected.

text.title: The Sourcing Gals refuse further deal conversations until the technology is protected.

circle.title: step: 02; label: Weigh venturing against licensing; value: Step 2; detail: Venturing meant floating at least $250,000 with retailers paying in 60 to 90 days (inventRightTV); Patent Question bars manufacturing without demand, margins, a sales channel and operating ability.

text.title: Venturing meant floating at least $250,000 with retailers paying in 60 to 90 days (inventRightTV); Patent Question bars manufacturing without demand, margins, a sales channel and operating ability.

circle.title: step: 03; label: Pitch as a product developer; value: Step 3; detail: Polished brochures, formal letters and prototypes; brokers paid on commission only and vetted through the United Inventors Association and Better Business Bureau (UpCounsel).

text.title: Polished brochures, formal letters and prototypes; brokers paid on commission only and vetted through the United Inventors Association and Better Business Bureau (UpCounsel).

circle.title: step: 04; label: Choose exclusivity and markets; value: Step 4; detail: Pick an exclusive partner carefully or demand non-exclusive where you hold market power (Patent pc); license human and pet markets at once (Licensing Consulting Group).

text.title: Pick an exclusive partner carefully or demand non-exclusive where you hold market power (Patent pc); license human and pet markets at once (Licensing Consulting Group).

circle.title: step: 05; label: Set minimums, then price; value: Step 5; detail: No license without annual minimums (Michigan Engineering); price comes last and is capped by the licensee's next best alternative (Kauffman FoundersSchool).

text.title: No license without annual minimums (Michigan Engineering); price comes last and is capped by the licensee's next best alternative (Kauffman FoundersSchool).

Assumptions: Step order follows the operator gates cited for Chapter Q1. Royalty bands are attributed claims (2 to 10% of wholesale per Patent Question, 3 to 5% and up to 10% per Patent pc, 5 to 20% per UpCounsel) and vary by industry.
